## Scope of the artifact

The document lists capabilities and acceptance criteria, but does not define entities, field constraints, API contracts, or UI behavior. Almost every implementation choice would currently be invented rather than specified.

---

## Ambiguities

### 1. Ticket ID format

**Question:** What is a ticket identifier? Human-readable (`TKT-0001`), UUID, database integer, or something else? Is it assigned at create time, and is it immutable and unique?

**Why it matters:** IDs drive URLs, search, logs, and uniqueness. Integer IDs leak volume; UUIDs are ugly in the UI; sequential codes need a generator and gap policy.

**Reasonable option:** Server-generated immutable string `TKT-{zero-padded sequence}`.

**Consequence:** Requires a unique sequence (or equivalent) in the database, and list/detail APIs must expose that string as the public ID.

---

### 2. Required versus optional fields

**Question:** On create and update, which of title, description, priority, assignee, status, comments are required? Can description be empty? Can a ticket be created with only a title?

**Why it matters:** Backend validation, UI form layout, and error messages all depend on this. “Validate input” is meaningless without a required/optional matrix.

**Reasonable option:** Create requires non-blank title, description, and priority; assignee optional; status not client-set (defaults to `OPEN`); comments created separately.

**Consequence:** Create API must reject missing title/description/priority; UI must mark those fields required and omit status from the create form.

---

### 3. Title length

**Question:** What are min/max title length, and is whitespace trimmed before measuring?

**Why it matters:** UI layout, database column size, and validation errors. Unbounded titles break lists; a 1-character title is usually noise.

**Reasonable option:** Trim whitespace; length 3–120 characters.

**Consequence:** Backend rejects shorter/longer titles; UI needs a counter and a specific error string.

---

### 4. Description length

**Question:** Min/max description length? Plain text only, or markdown/HTML? Are blank descriptions allowed?

**Why it matters:** Storage, XSS if HTML is allowed, and whether “empty ticket body” is valid.

**Reasonable option:** Optional plain text, max 5,000 characters, no HTML.

**Consequence:** Need sanitization or reject markup; UI textarea with a hard limit; DB column sized accordingly.

---

### 5. Priority values

**Question:** What are the allowed priority values? Ordered enum (`LOW`/`MEDIUM`/`HIGH`/`CRITICAL`) or free text? Default if omitted?

**Why it matters:** Filtering, sorting, and validation. Free text cannot be sorted or filtered reliably.

**Reasonable option:** Required enum: `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`. No default; client must send one.

**Consequence:** Invalid priority is a 400; UI is a select, not a text box; sorting by priority is well-defined.

---

### 6. Assignee representation

**Question:** Is assignee a free-text name, email, user ID, or a User entity? Display name vs identifier?

**Why it matters:** Identity, uniqueness, and whether “change assignee” means picking from a directory or typing a string.

**Reasonable option:** Assignee is a user ID referencing a User record; API also returns display name.

**Consequence:** Requires a user (or agent) catalog and a foreign-key (or equivalent) check on assign.

---

### 7. Whether an unassigned ticket is allowed

**Question:** May `assignee` be null at create? May it be cleared later? Must every `IN_PROGRESS` ticket have an assignee?

The requirements file is named `spec/requirments.md` rather than `spec/requirements.md`.

The project steering rules are the system prompt's always-applied workspace rules. The architecture document will cite both the requirements file and these rules. It will propose the full Spring Boot and React/Next.js stack without deciding product requirements. It will flag decisions needing confirmation. It will explicitly explain state-machine enforcement and how the design prevents callers from bypassing ticket state transitions. The document will follow existing patterns, prioritize branch safety, and explain all changes clearly.

Secure coding defaults will prohibit eval, hardcoded credentials, permissive CORS, and authentication bypasses. Dependency discipline, minimal changes, and secrets protection will govern the design. The architecture proposes a monorepo with a Spring Boot backend and a Next.js frontend. The proposed layer stack is five-tier: API/Controller for HTTP mapping and DTO binding; Service for orchestration and transactions; Domain for the Ticket aggregate and StatusTransitionPolicy; Repository for persistence only; and Persistence using JPA with PostgreSQL in production and H2 for testing.

State machine enforcement will be centralized on the backend. A dedicated transition endpoint will handle status changes, while general PATCH and PUT operations will ignore status updates. The domain policy will serve as the single source of truth, and repositories will not be allowed to mutate status independently. Controllers will not persist tickets directly. Database CHECK constraints and optimistic locking will guard against invalid transitions. Integration tests will verify that callers cannot bypass the state machine.

The transition endpoint will be a dedicated POST route accepting a target status. The Ticket entity will expose only a package-private or method-only `transitionStatus(to)` that consults the domain policy, with no public setter for status. JPA lifecycle events will restrict mutations to the domain method, and the service layer will remain the sole transactional writer. An optional database trigger may be added, but it will be flagged for confirmation.

The Next.js frontend will use the App Router, call the Spring API through an API client, and read the API base URL from environment variables. CORS will be configured, and the frontend will display errors returned by the API.

Spring will support three profiles—local, test, and production—with credentials kept in environment variables and never committed to version control. The configuration will use `application.yml` placeholders.

Testing will include unit tests for the state machine, slice tests for controllers, integration tests against H2 or Testcontainers, and frontend tests. Product ambiguities from the prior review will be flagged as pending confirmation, since the architecture document does not decide product rules. The file will be created as `spec/architecture.md`.

The architecture document will use mermaid diagrams and conceptual type names instead of full implementation code. Two design choices still need confirmation: whether Next.js should run as an App Router or a Pages Router, and whether the database migration tool should be Flyway or Liquibase. The proposed package structure is traditional layered, with a dedicated domain package isolating the state machine from other layers. Authentication is not explicitly required by the original requirements, though the steering rules forbid authentication bypasses.

The architecture will assume an open API for local and development environments until authentication requirements are clarified. Production CORS will remain strict and non-permissive.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I will read the approved requirements and draft a formal state-machine specification. The document will define valid and invalid transitions between all five ticket states. It will include a transition table, explicit business rules, and API error semantics. The goal is to provide enough detail for developers to write direct unit and integration tests.

There are 25 possible state-to-state transitions across the five states. The allowed transitions are OPEN→IN_PROGRESS, IN_PROGRESS→RESOLVED, RESOLVED→CLOSED, OPEN→CANCELLED, and IN_PROGRESS→CANCELLED. All remaining 20 pairs must be explicitly marked as invalid. Each entry in the transition table will list the current state, requested state, validity, and reason.

Self-transitions are invalid because the allowed set does not include identity edges. The OPEN state cannot advance to RESOLVED; that path is skipped. Every remaining pair is explicitly classified as invalid.

OPEN→CLOSED is invalid. IN_PROGRESS→OPEN, IN_PROGRESS→CLOSED, and IN_PROGRESS→IN_PROGRESS are invalid. RESOLVED→OPEN, RESOLVED→IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED→RESOLVED, and RESOLVED→CANCELLED are invalid. CLOSED→OPEN, CLOSED→IN_PROGRESS, CLOSED→RESOLVED, and CLOSED→CLOSED are invalid.

CANCELLED is terminal. All transitions from CANCELLED are invalid. The specification must choose one HTTP status code for invalid transitions. The architecture leaves 409 versus 422 unresolved. The chosen code will be testable.

The specification will define a dedicated transition operation. Invalid transitions must be rejected, nothing persisted, and an error returned. The HTTP status code will be 409 Conflict. This choice is selected over 422 Unprocessable Entity because the conflict is a business rule on the current state rather than a semantic validation failure.

The error response will carry HTTP 409 Conflict. It will contain a machine-readable code ILLEGAL_STATUS_TRANSITION, a human-readable message naming the current and requested states, and guarantee that the ticket status remains unchanged. A malformed status value returns 400 Bad Request. A missing ticket returns 404 Not Found. Updating the status field directly without invoking the transition endpoint returns 400 Bad Request.

Tickets are created in the OPEN state. The backend must reject any creation request that supplies an initial status other than OPEN. Test scenarios will follow a given/when/then format without implementation code. Terminal states have no outgoing edges. UI button visibility is treated as a presentation concern; tests must exercise the backend transition endpoint directly.
</details></think>

# Senior Architect Review — Support Ticket Management System

**Scope reviewed:** `spec/requirments.md`, `spec/architecture.md`, `spec/data-model.md`, `spec/state-machine.md`, `spec/ui-flow.md`, `spec/test-strategy.md`  
**Not reviewed (missing):** `spec/requirements.md`, `spec/api-contract.md`  
**Verdict:** **Not ready for implementation.** Internal consistency is good in places, but several **Critical** gaps remain — especially the missing API contract, unapproved product rules that downstream docs treat as fixed, and a state-machine bypass surface that is only partially closed.

---

## Critical

| Severity | File | Issue | Why it matters | Recommended correction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Critical** | `spec/api-contract.md` (missing) | **No API contract exists.** Architecture, UI flows, and test strategy all reference “conceptual” endpoints, error codes, and query parameters that have no authoritative definition. | Without a contract, implementers will invent paths, verbs, request/response shapes, and error fields independently. The state-machine bypass protections (e.g. “field update must not accept `status`”) cannot be verified against a real contract. | Create `spec/api-contract.md` before any code. Define every endpoint, method, request/response schema, query params, and the exact error JSON shape. Explicitly state: (1) update endpoint rejects `status`; (2) create endpoint rejects or ignores `status`; (3) transition endpoint accepts only `requestedStatus`. |
| **Critical** | `spec/requirments.md` | **The “requirements analysis” was never produced.** The file contains the raw prompt, not the analysis it asks for (functional/non-functional requirements, validation rules, ambiguities, assumptions). | Downstream documents (`data-model.md`, `state-machine.md`, `ui-flow.md`) cite this as the source of truth, but the actual product decisions (required fields, lengths, priority values, assignee model, search semantics, pagination) were never made. | Produce the requirements analysis the prompt requested. Resolve every ambiguity listed in the earlier review (ticket ID format, required vs optional fields, title/description length, priority values, assignee representation, unassigned allowed, comment rules, search behavior, case sensitivity, partial vs exact, status filter behavior, pagination, sorting, error format, date/time, database behavior, status editability, comment edit/delete, assignee existence). |
| **Critical** | `spec/state-machine.md` §7.2 | **Error schema is defined only for illegal transitions.** The global error JSON schema (`code`, `message`, `fieldErrors`?) is marked “requires confirmation” in architecture §9 but is treated as fixed in state-machine §7.2 and test-strategy §8.3. | Tests will assert exact `code` strings (`ILLEGAL_STATUS_TRANSITION`, `STATUS_NOT_UPDATABLE`, etc.) that were never approved as a contract. If the API contract later chooses different codes, all state-machine and UI tests break. | Approve a single error schema in the API contract. State-machine doc should reference it, not define it unilaterally. |
| **Critical** | `spec/state-machine.md` §2, §7.3 | **Create-time status injection is ambiguous.** “Either the create contract omits `status`, or a supplied non-`OPEN` value is rejected as invalid input (HTTP 400).” Two different behaviors are allowed. | One implementation may silently ignore `status: CLOSED` on create; another may 400. Tests cannot assert a single behavior. This is a state-machine bypass surface: if create silently ignores status, a caller could probe whether it was honored. | Pick one: create contract **omits** `status` entirely (preferred — unknown property → 400), or create accepts `status` but rejects any value other than `OPEN`. Document the choice in the API contract. |
| **Critical** | `spec/architecture.md` §10.2, `spec/state-machine.md` §4 | **State-machine bypass via repository is only prevented by convention.** “Controllers cannot reach repositories” and “entities do not expose a public status setter” are design rules, not enforced constraints. | A future developer can add a repository method or a public setter and bypass the domain policy. No test or architectural guard prevents this. | Add an architecture test (e.g. ArchUnit) that fails if any controller references a repository, or if any entity exposes a public `setStatus`. Alternatively, make the status field package-private and only mutable via the domain transition method. Document this as a required test in `test-strategy.md`. |

## Major

| Severity | File | Issue | Why it matters | Recommended correction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Major** | `spec/data-model.md` §2.1 | **Ticket `id` type is unresolved** (UUID vs sequence vs display code). | Every test fixture, API path, and frontend route depends on this. H2 vs PostgreSQL behavior differs for UUID vs identity. | Decide in the requirements analysis. If UUID, state whether it is DB-generated or app-generated. |
| **Major** | `spec/data-model.md` §4 | **Assignee representation is unresolved.** Three options are listed; none chosen. | The API contract cannot define the assignee field type. The UI cannot know whether to render a text input or a user picker. “Assignee must already exist” cannot be tested. | Choose option A (free-text), B (opaque id), or C (users table) in the requirements analysis. If C, define the users table. |
| **Major** | `spec/data-model.md` §6 | **Priority values are a proposal, not approved.** | The data model, API contract, and UI all need the exact set. Tests cannot assert valid/invalid priority. | Approve or reject the proposed `LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL` set in the requirements analysis. |
| **Major** | `spec/state-machine.md` §7.2 vs `spec/architecture.md` §9 | **HTTP status for illegal transition is 409 in state-machine, “409 or 422” in architecture.** | Architecture says “requires confirmation”; state-machine says “standardizes on 409.” These are contradictory. | Architecture should defer to state-machine (409) once the API contract is approved. Remove the “or 422” from architecture. |
| **Major** | `spec/ui-flow.md` §11.2 | **UI shows only “suggested” transitions, but the suggestion table is not derived from the backend.** | If the backend adds a new edge (e.g. `RESOLVED → CANCELLED`), the UI will not show it until manually updated. The UI and backend can drift. | The API should expose the allowed transitions for the current ticket state (e.g. `allowedTransitions: ["IN_PROGRESS", "CANCELLED"]` in the ticket response). The UI renders from that list, not from a hardcoded table. |
| **Major** | `spec/test-strategy.md` §7 | **State-machine integration tests do not cover concurrent transitions.** | Two simultaneous `OPEN → IN_PROGRESS` and `OPEN → CANCELLED` requests could both succeed if optimistic locking is not implemented. The spec mentions locking as “requires confirmation” but never requires a test for it. | Either confirm optimistic locking and add a concurrency test, or explicitly accept last-write-wins and document the risk. |
| **Major** | `spec/test-strategy.md` §10 | **“No secrets committed” has no test.** | The acceptance criterion exists, but no test, scan, or CI check is defined. | Add a CI step (e.g. `gitleaks`, `trufflehog`) or a pre-commit hook. Document it in test-strategy. |
| **Major** | `spec/architecture.md` §11 | **CORS and auth are unresolved but the UI flow assumes browser → backend communication.** | If CORS is misconfigured or auth is added later, all frontend flows break. The spec says “local/dev may run without user identity only as an explicit temporary decision” but never defines that decision. | Decide: (1) CORS direct vs Next.js proxy; (2) auth model or explicit “no auth in v1.” Document in API contract and architecture. |

```
### 3.1 Interpretations of the written machine (flagged for product confirmation)

The written requirements list the allowed edges and three invalid examples but do not state every rule explicitly. The following are **interpretations** that follow from “only listed edges are valid.” They are part of this contract unless the product owner changes them; changing any of them is a requirements change, not an implementation detail.

| # | Interpretation | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I-1 | Same-state requests (`X → X`) are invalid, not idempotent success | No same-state edge is listed |
| I-2 | `RESOLVED → CANCELLED` is invalid | Only `OPEN → CANCELLED` and `IN_PROGRESS → CANCELLED` are listed |
| I-3 | `CLOSED` and `CANCELLED` are terminal (no outbound edges) | No outbound edges are listed for them |
| I-4 | `OPEN` is the only initial status | Requirements define creation but no initial-status choice |
| I-5 | Illegal transitions return **409** (not 422) | Standardized in §7.2 so tests have one expected status |

---

## 4. Business rule — status is not a field update
```

```
Every SM case asserts: HTTP status, JSON `code`, `currentStatus` / `requestedStatus` on 409, and persisted status via GET.

### 7.5 Architecture-guard tests

Automated tests (e.g. ArchUnit or equivalent) that fail the build if the layering and bypass rules in `spec/architecture.md` §2 and §10 are violated:

| # | Rule under test |
| --- | --- |
| AG-1 | Controllers do not reference repositories |
| AG-2 | Repositories do not contain transition logic |
| AG-3 | Ticket status is mutated only through the domain transition operation (no public status setter usable by API/service code) |
| AG-4 | Services do not perform ad-hoc status updates |

These tests enforce rules that already exist in the specifications; they add no new product behavior.

---

## 8. Frontend tests
```

```
## 12. Search and filtering test data

Reference seed set (test fixture, not product data):

| # | Title | Description | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T1 | `Login page crashes` | `Crash on submit` | `OPEN` |
| T2 | `Password reset broken` | `Email never arrives` | `IN_PROGRESS` |
| T3 | `Login logo missing` | `Asset 404` | `RESOLVED` |
| T4 | `Old SSO issue` | `Superseded` | `CLOSED` |
| T5 | `Duplicate signup` | `Created twice` | `CANCELLED` |

- Search: positive match (`Login` → T1, T3), negative match (`billing` → none). Case-sensitivity and partial-vs-exact assertions must be written **only after** the product decision on search semantics; until then those assertions are placeholders, not passing criteria.  
- Filter: each status returns exactly its one ticket; “all” returns five.  
- Combined search + filter: only if the API contract defines it.
```

# Corrections Applied

## 1. Filename inconsistency (structural)

- **Original issue:** every prompt and spec referenced `spec/requirements.md`, but the file on disk was `spec/requirments.md`.
- **Correction:** renamed `spec/requirments.md` → `spec/requirements.md`; updated the "Sources" header in `architecture.md`, `data-model.md`, `state-machine.md`, `ui-flow.md`, `test-strategy.md`, plus two inline references (`data-model.md` closing note, `ui-flow.md` §2 rule 4). No content of the requirements file was changed.
- **Consistency:** grep confirms zero remaining `requirments.md` references in `spec/`.

## 2. 409 vs 422 contradiction (Critical/Major)

- **Original issue:** `architecture.md` §9 said "409 or 422 (requires confirmation)"; `state-machine.md` §7.2 said "standardizes on 409."
- **Correction:** `architecture.md` §9 now states **409**, defined in `state-machine.md` §7.2; §16 item 5 marked decided. The only remaining `422` mentions are in `state-machine.md`, where they document the decision rationale.
- **Consistency:** `ui-flow.md` §11/§13 and `test-strategy.md` §7 already asserted 409 — now all four documents agree.

## 3. Create-time status ambiguity (Critical — bypass surface)

- **Original issue:** `state-machine.md` §2 allowed two behaviors ("omit `status`" **or** "reject non-`OPEN`"), so implementations could diverge and tests could not assert one behavior.
- **Correction:** standardized on the stricter, verifiable option — the create contract has **no** `status` field; if present → **400 `STATUS_NOT_UPDATABLE`**, no ticket persisted. Updated: `state-machine.md` §2, §7.3 (new row), §8.2 (new test 21); `architecture.md` §8 (create rule alongside the update rule); `test-strategy.md` §5 (create row) and new **SM-33**; `ui-flow.md` §12 (`STATUS_NOT_UPDATABLE` row now covers create and edit).
- **Consistency:** the same code (`STATUS_NOT_UPDATABLE`) now governs create and update in all documents; the error code set is unchanged — no new codes invented.

## 4. Error-schema ownership contradiction (Critical)

- **Original issue:** `architecture.md` §9 marked the error schema "requires confirmation" while `state-machine.md` §7.2 and `test-strategy.md` treated the codes as fixed.
- **Correction:** `architecture.md` §9 and §16 item 6 now name `state-machine.md` §7 as the source of truth for lifecycle error codes until `spec/api-contract.md` exists. No codes were changed.
- **Consistency:** grep confirms the five codes (`ILLEGAL_STATUS_TRANSITION`, `STATUS_NOT_UPDATABLE`, `INVALID_STATUS_VALUE`, `INVALID_REQUEST`, `TICKET_NOT_FOUND`) appear with identical spelling across `state-machine.md`, `test-strategy.md`, `ui-flow.md`, `architecture.md`.

## 5. State-machine bypass only prevented by convention (Critical)

- **Original issue:** "controllers cannot reach repositories" and "no public status setter" were design rules with no enforcement mechanism.
- **Correction:** added **architecture-guard tests** (AG-1…AG-4) in `test-strategy.md` §7.5, a matching row in the §1 levels table, a bypass-table row in `architecture.md` §10.2, and a §13 testing-architecture row. These enforce rules that already existed — no new product behavior.
- **Consistency:** `architecture.md` §10.2 and §13 cross-reference `test-strategy.md` §7.5; verified by grep.

## 6. Unapproved assumptions now explicit (Major)

- **Original issue:** same-state invalid, `RESOLVED → CANCELLED` invalid, terminal states, `OPEN`-only initial, and 409 were embedded as silent interpretations.
- **Correction:** new `state-machine.md` §3.1 lists all five as **flagged interpretations** (I-1…I-5) with their basis, stating that changing any of them is a requirements change. No behavior changed.
- **Consistency:** §3.1 matches the §5 transition table exactly (25 pairs unchanged).

## 7. Concurrency test gap (Major)

- **Correction:** new **SM-34** in `test-strategy.md` §7.4 — required if optimistic locking is confirmed; otherwise `architecture.md` must document the accepted last-write-wins risk. Conditional, so it does not smuggle in the locking decision.

## 8. "No secrets committed" unverifiable (Major)

- **Correction:** `test-strategy.md` §10 now requires a CI secret-scanning step to pass on every commit. This makes an existing acceptance criterion verifiable; it adds no product requirement.

## 9. UI/backend transition-table drift (Major)

- **Correction:** `ui-flow.md` §11.2 gained a **sync rule**: the suggested-actions table must mirror `state-machine.md` §5, and server-provided `allowedTransitions` is recorded as a *requires-confirmation* option — not adopted.

## 10. Minor corrections

- **Vague search test data:** `test-strategy.md` §12 now has a concrete 5-ticket seed fixture; case/partial assertions explicitly remain placeholders until the product decides search semantics.
- **Client-side validation floor:** `ui-flow.md` §12 now states client checks must never be stricter than the backend.

## False positive in the review (no change)

- The review claimed `STATUS_NOT_UPDATABLE` was not asserted in the test strategy. It was (SM-28). No correction needed.

## Deliberately NOT corrected (would silently introduce requirements)

- Missing `spec/api-contract.md` — creating it requires path/schema decisions; still blocking.
- Missing requirements analysis (priority values, assignee model, ID format, field lengths, search semantics, pagination, comment mutability, unassigned tickets) — product decisions, still blocking.
- CORS vs BFF and auth model — still open decisions in `architecture.md` §16.

## Cross-document consistency check

- Filename references: clean.
- HTTP codes: 400/404/409/500 used identically everywhere; no stray 422/204 contracts.
- Error codes: identical spelling in all four documents that use them.
- Transition rules: `state-machine.md` §5 = `ui-flow.md` §11.2 = `test-strategy.md` §7 (5 valid / 20 invalid, terminal states, same-state invalid).
- Create/update `status` rejection: `state-machine.md` §2/§7.3 = `architecture.md` §8 = `test-strategy.md` §5/SM-33 = `ui-flow.md` §3/§12.
- Unresolved markers (`requires confirmation`/`unresolved`) remain only where a genuine product/architecture decision is pending — none were resolved silently.

The api-contract.md file is missing. I will proceed with implementation.

An in-memory repository will back the service layer. The REST controller will expose endpoints for creation, retrieval, field updates, and explicit status transitions. PATCH will reject status changes. A dedicated endpoint will handle transitions. Business exceptions will return 400, 404, or 409. Tests will use MockMvc against the in-memory store.

A ConcurrentHashMap-backed TicketStore will serve as the in-memory repository. The service layer will enforce all status transitions, while the REST controller will reject direct status updates to prevent API bypasses. Tests will cover every valid transition, representative invalid transitions, and attempts to bypass the rule through field updates. A Clock bean is also required.

Jackson will be configured to fail on unknown properties. This prevents clients from injecting a status field during ticket creation and ensures the server rejects it with a 400 error.

Jackson will reject status fields during deserialization by throwing a custom `StatusNotUpdatableException` from the DTO setters. This prevents API callers from injecting a status value even when Jackson is configured to ignore unknown properties. Response DTOs are also being defined.

The package layout is now defined. Application code will live under `application`, persistence under `persistence`, and API concerns under `api`. The repository interface will reside in the application package. The `TicketResponse` record carries the ticket identifier, title, description, priority, assignee, status, and timestamps. The `TransitionRequest` DTO will explicitly reject a `status` field to prevent injection. Existing domain tests will be preserved.

A @SpringBootTest with @AutoConfigureMockMvc will be used for the transition API tests. This ensures the business rule cannot be bypassed by API callers. H2 is unnecessary because the task is scoped to the state machine. The web starter must be added to the POM. The JSON mapper needs to serialize TicketStatus as a string. The existing exceptions, TicketTest, and POM will be reviewed next.

Domain exceptions are needed for invalid status updates and invalid requests.

The controller advice will return HTTP 409 for illegal transitions and HTTP 400 for malformed requests. Tests will use @SpringBootTest with @AutoConfigureMockMvc. The in-memory repository needs a reset between tests; a visible-for-testing clear method is preferred over @DirtiesContext.

**Specs read:** `spec/requirements.md`, `spec/state-machine.md`, `spec/test-strategy.md`. **`spec/api-contract.md` is not in the repo**; HTTP codes/bodies follow `state-machine.md` §7.

## What was implemented

Status is **not** a field update. Changes go only through:

1. Domain `Ticket.transitionTo` + `TicketStatusPolicy` (five allowed edges)
2. `TicketService.transition` (load → domain rule → save)
3. `POST /api/tickets/{id}/transitions` with `{ "requestedStatus": "..." }`

Bypass paths:

- `PATCH /api/tickets/{id}` with `status` → **400** `STATUS_NOT_UPDATABLE`
- `POST /api/tickets` with `status` → **400** `STATUS_NOT_UPDATABLE`

Illegal edges → **409** `ILLEGAL_STATUS_TRANSITION` with `currentStatus` / `requestedStatus`. Unknown label → **400** `INVALID_STATUS_VALUE`. Missing ticket → **404** `TICKET_NOT_FOUND`.

No frontend changes. Persistence is **in-memory** (not PostgreSQL/H2 yet).

## Tests run

```text
source "$HOME/.sdkman/bin/sdkman-init.sh"
export JAVA_HOME=.../java/21.0.8-tem
mvn -f backend/pom.xml test
```

| `TicketServiceTransitionTest` | 14 |
| Domain policy/aggregate | 67 |

First `mvn test` had **1 failure** (`missingTicket` expected `$.currentStatus` on 404). Spec only requires those fields on **409**. Assertion was fixed; re-run passed.

## Assumptions

- Paths `/api/tickets` and `/transitions` until an API contract exists
- Create HTTP **201**; valid transition **200**
- In-memory store for this task only

**Endpoints (requirements only)**

| Use case | Method | Path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create | `POST` | `/api/tickets` |
| List, search (`q`), filter (`status`) | `GET` | `/api/tickets` |
| Get | `GET` | `/api/tickets/{ticketId}` |
| Update title/description/priority/assignee | `PATCH` | `/api/tickets/{ticketId}` |
| Change status | `POST` | `/api/tickets/{ticketId}/transitions` |
| Add comment | `POST` | `/api/tickets/{ticketId}/comments` |

**State machine**
- Create and PATCH **forbid** `status` → 400 `STATUS_NOT_UPDATABLE`
- Transitions use `requestedStatus` only; domain evaluates allowed edges
- Illegal pair → 409 `ILLEGAL_STATUS_TRANSITION` with `code`, `message`, `currentStatus`, `requestedStatus`
- Unknown label → 400 `INVALID_STATUS_VALUE`; missing ticket → 404 `TICKET_NOT_FOUND`

**Consistency**
- All errors use the same JSON object
- Responses are DTOs, not persistence entities
- No delete, auth, pagination, or other extra resources

Still open in product specs (called out, not invented): field lengths, priority enum, search case/partial rules, assignee directory.

The backend is the only place that decides status changes. `TicketStatusPolicy` allows exactly five edges; `Ticket.transitionTo` and `TicketService.transition` apply that table before persist. Create always starts `OPEN`. Field updates cannot change status. No new REST controllers were added.

**Allowed**
- `OPEN` → `IN_PROGRESS`
- `IN_PROGRESS` → `RESOLVED`
- `RESOLVED` → `CLOSED`
- `OPEN` → `CANCELLED`
- `IN_PROGRESS` → `CANCELLED`

Every other pair, including same-state, is `ILLEGAL_STATUS_TRANSITION`. Unknown labels (wrong case such as `open`) are `INVALID_STATUS_VALUE`. Null or blank requested status is `INVALID_REQUEST` at the service. On rejection, status and `updatedAt` stay unchanged.

The ticket **service** now owns the required operations and returns application DTOs (`TicketDetailDto`, `TicketSummaryDto`, `CommentDto`). Controllers map those to REST responses. JPA entities are not returned.

**Operations** (`TicketService`, `@Transactional` on writes, `readOnly` on reads):
- **Create** — always `OPEN`; `status` in the request is rejected; blank title is `INVALID_REQUEST`
- **Get** — 404 `TICKET_NOT_FOUND` if missing; comments included in detail
- **List / search / filter** — `q` and `status` combine with **AND**; blank `q` is no keyword constraint; invalid `status` is `INVALID_STATUS_VALUE`; empty result is an empty list
- **Update fields** — title/description/priority/assignee only; omitted optionals stay stored; explicit `null` clears; `status` present is `STATUS_NOT_UPDATABLE` with no mutation
- **Change status** — domain policy only; illegal pairs do not persist
- **Add comment** — blank body rejected; ticket `status` and `updatedAt` unchanged

Search is documented as **case-insensitive partial match** on title or description (same portable rule as the JPA repository).

**Tests:** `TicketServiceTest` (create/get/list/search/filter/update/comment success and failure) and `TicketServiceTransitionTest` (all 25 pairs). `mvn test` passed.

The api-contract specifies a consistent error DTO with code and message fields. Status codes include 400 for invalid requests and malformed JSON, 409 for state transitions, and 500 for server errors. Stack traces, SQL, and secrets must remain hidden. Validation failures will be handled via MethodArgumentNotValidException and ConstraintViolationException. Controllers currently lack @Valid annotations.

A minimal approach avoids adding @Valid annotations to request DTOs to respect the "do not modify unrelated functionality" constraint. The exception handler will instead catch MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException for invalid UUIDs, MethodArgumentNotValidException and ConstraintViolationException for validation failures, and MissingServletRequestParameterException. All will return 400 INVALID_REQUEST with stable, non-sensitive messages.

Persistence-related exceptions will return 500 without codes or internal details. Generic exceptions will also return 500 with stable messages. A HandlerExceptionResolver will handle type mismatches on path variables. IllegalArgumentException messages are safe to return since they are domain-specific. Malformed JSON is already covered by HttpMessageNotReadableException.

Spring Boot error configuration will be disabled to prevent stack traces and internal messages from appearing in responses.

The API error response DTO uses JsonInclude NON_NULL to omit the code field on 500 errors.

Tests will verify 404 for unknown tickets, 400 for invalid UUIDs and malformed JSON, 400 for blank titles, 400 for invalid status values, and 400 for invalid state transitions.

A 409 error will include currentStatus and requestedStatus for illegal state transitions. Persistence errors will be tested with @WebMvcTest and a mocked TicketService throwing DataAccessException. This avoids modifying the service layer while verifying 500 responses.

Existing TicketTransitionApiTest will be extended for reachable HTTP errors. A dedicated @WebMvcTest will mock TicketService to throw DataAccessException and verify 500 responses. YAML will disable stack traces, messages, and binding errors entirely.

HandlerMethodValidationException will be caught alongside the other validation exceptions. UUID type mismatches will return a specific "Ticket id is invalid." message, while other invalid requests will fall back to "Request is invalid."

Server-side logging will capture unexpected error stack traces, but responses will never include exception messages. For 500 errors, the API error response will omit the code field entirely and return a stable non-secret message such as "An unexpected error occurred." IllegalArgumentException messages are acceptable only if they are user-safe; domain-specific messages like "Title must not be blank" are fine, but SQL-related exceptions must be suppressed.

IllegalArgumentException will always return the stable message "Request is invalid." at the HTTP boundary. This prevents any risk of leaking internal exception details. The existing domain-specific message "Title must not be blank" is preserved only because blank titles currently trigger InvalidRequestException from the service layer rather than IllegalArgumentException.

API errors now go through a single `ApiExceptionHandler` and the contract shape in `spec/api-contract.md`. `rules/api-standards.md` is not in the repo; mapping follows the contract plus architecture §9.

**Response shape** (`code`, `message`; `currentStatus` / `requestedStatus` only on illegal transitions):

| Case | HTTP | `code` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ticket not found | 404 | `TICKET_NOT_FOUND` |
| Malformed JSON, invalid UUID, blank/missing required fields, bean-validation | 400 | `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Unknown status label (e.g. `open`) | 400 | `INVALID_STATUS_VALUE` |
| `status` on create/PATCH | 400 | `STATUS_NOT_UPDATABLE` |
| Illegal lifecycle pair | 409 | `ILLEGAL_STATUS_TRANSITION` |
| Optimistic lock | 409 | omitted |
| Persistence / unexpected failure | 500 | omitted; message `An unexpected error occurred.` |

Bodies do not include stack traces, SQL, JDBC URLs, or exception class names. Server error pages are configured not to include those details.

Create/update require a non-blank `title` (`@Valid` + `@NotBlank`) so validation failures hit the same 400 path.

**Tests:** `ApiExceptionHandlingTest` (HTTP status + JSON for 400/404/409 cases) and `ApiPersistenceExceptionHandlingTest` (500/optimistic lock without internals). `mvn test` passed.
